facts.statement: DSpark1584 writes the known seed to T[:,0]. Step i uses markov_embed(T[:,i]), Markov bias, BF16 in-place base+bias add, greedy argmax/remap and copies prediction into T[:,i+1]. Observed five steps do not mean the seed is a discarded prediction. Early-return DSpark1637/1643 returns T[:,1:].

Merged1454-1780 also contains probability/draft_probs, selector, non-DSpark and autoregressive-continuation branches. Current trace positives bind the greedy Markov path; actual parallel/dynamic configs remain unrecorded. _propose also has a num_speculative_tokens0 return. Do not promote count/absence to all flags.

DSpark1611-1617 calls dynamic_spec.update after the Markov loop with model,last_hidden_states,draft_token_ids,num_reqs. DynamicSpecScheduler in spec_decode/utils.py is the actual imported receiver; method-name-only search for confidence missed receiver.update.

DSpark confidence uses raw last_hidden_states.reshape(B*D,H), and model.markov_embed(T[:B,:D]) including the seed and previous predictions. This is the same ordered embedding-input sequence as the loop under one parameter/input generation, not the just-produced T[:,1:D+1] sequence.

Confidence head is ReplicatedLinear(H+R,1,params_dtype=float32,bias=False in this DSpark constructor). It concatenates raw hidden and embedding after embedding-to-hidden-dtype conversion, widens toFP32, projects once and applies sigmoid. It does not apply the base LM-head RMSNorm to hidden.

Scheduler copies probability into a persistentFP32[B,D] bank and clamps to[1e-6,1]. It computes FP32cumprod survival, updates shared budget, then allocates keep lengths. NaN is not repaired by clamp; finite-domain monotonic arguments need their own condition.

Periodic budget increments its counter on each update; at interval resets the counter before checking B0. For B>0 it counts survival>=threshold via .sum().item(), divides byB,ceil, increments even budgets belowD, and clamps to[min_k,D]. The newly updated budget is used by allocation in that same call. Defaults are configuration defaults, not actual captured values.

Allocator fills min_k per request, globally TopKs B*max(budget_k-min_k,0) candidates from flattened survival[:,min_k:] (bounded by candidate count), converts positions to request IDs by floor-div and scatter-adds counts. It is not independent per-request thresholding or a uniform fixedbudget per row.

Global TopK is sorted=False. Flat order, boundary ties, finite/NaN/underflow behavior and per-request count outcomes matter; a new selection/histogram protocol cannot arbitrarily reassign equal-score winners.

take_draft_token_ids2205-2226 retrieves out, returns it unchanged if no dynamic scheduler/result, otherwise converts each device k with int(k), clamps[0,self.num_spec_tokens], then tokens[:k] through zip. It trims already-generated lists at retrieval; it does not stop Markov generation. Vector/order/generation and current zip behavior must be preserved.

Next-ID helper2192-2252 unconditionally constructs backup IDs from requests.get_token_id(num_tokens_no_spec-1) and copies the backup bank toGPU. It clones sampled IDs, fills discard rows with-1, counts literal(x!=-1)&(x<V), gathers count-1 clamped to0, and chooses backup when count0. Original sampled IDs remain unmodified.

The helper returns INT32 next IDs and INT64 counts for current typed domains. Native BOOL->FLOATsum->INT64 counts at K1/6 are exactly0..K. A fused integer count can preserve these bounded results; do not generalize unbounded shape/overflow behavior.

worker2033 passes both next/count to _copy_valid_sampled_token_count and to input preparation/proposal. The copy helper returns immediately if eventNone; otherwise a named copy stream waits on default, copies counts toCPU non-blocking and records an event. Async mode retains the GPU count reference; input_batch.prev_sampled_token_ids then receives next IDs.

Count CPU copy, GPU correction reference and next-ID state are distinct consumers with readiness/last-reader requirements. Direct sampler summaries must preserve discard/vocab filtering and both returned dtypes; accepted_count+1 alone is not this contract.

Actual confidence/dynamic/parallel flags, ID/mask/slot values, repeated-ID hits, host scalar/copy costs, request-generation envelopes, native tie/precision details and causal gain remain unrecorded by this selector.
